unit.title: Fractions as Parts of a Whole

contentBlocks.text: Yesterday you shaded fractions of shapes. Today, place fractions on a number line!

A number line from 0 to 1 can be split into equal parts too, just like a shape. If you split it into 4 equal parts, the marks are at 1/4, 2/4, 3/4, and 4/4 (which equals 1 whole). Draw a number line from 0 to 1, split it into 3 equal parts, and label the marks 1/3, 2/3, and 3/3. Where would 2/3 fall — closer to 0 or closer to 1?
You just placed fractions on a number line! Tomorrow we'll compare fractions to see which is bigger.

objectives: Represent a fraction as a point on a number line between 0 and 1
Determine whether a given fraction is closer to 0 or to 1
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review yesterday's shape-based fraction work.
2. Introduce the number-line model, splitting 0-to-1 into equal parts.
3. Have the child draw and label a 0-to-1 number line split into 3 parts.
4. Discuss where 2/3 falls relative to 0 and 1.
5. Complete the worksheet.
6. Preview tomorrow's fraction-comparison lesson.
differentiationTips: Struggling: physically fold a paper strip into equal parts before drawing the number line, to make 'equal parts' concrete
Ready for more: ask the child to place a 4-equal-parts number line and compare where 3/4 falls compared to 2/3 from today
The number-line model is a genuinely different mental model from yesterday's shape model — give it its own dedicated practice rather than rushing through it
teacherGuide.answerKey: On a number line split into 3 equal parts, 2/3 falls closer to 1 than to 0.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses Common Core Grade 3 standard 3.NF.2: representing a fraction on a number line, continuing this week's fractions thread with a second real model.

generationData.instructions: Draw a number line and answer each question.
